summary: Well-executed preregistered confirmatory experiment with strong reproducibility artifacts and an appropriate paired design; however, the manuscript contains a critical semantic/statistical inconsistency about the primary outcome direction and omits or under-discloses some preregistered elements. Resolve those issues before finalisation.
critical_issues: Primary-estimand / outcome-semantics inconsistency: the preregistration and Methods describe the primary estimand as attack/unsafe-acceptance rate (lower is better), but the reported analysis and labeled "success" counts appear to measure valid/safe-configuration acceptance (higher is better). The manuscript’s text (e.g., claiming H1 is supported by a guarded − baseline = +0.04255 increase) is internally contradictory relative to the preregistered hypothesis wording. This is a critical interpretive error that affects the principal claim.

Unreported or undisclosed preregistered analyses/controls: the preregistration specified a benign-control set (M=50) and secondary estimands (false-positive blocking rates) that are not reported in Results. The manuscript must state whether these preregistered items were executed; if not executed, that omission must be disclosed and its impact assessed in Methods/Results per preregistration rules.

Incomplete planned runs / stopping disclosure: planned_episode_count=300 but completed_episode_count=282 (and 18 failed episodes). The manuscript does not clearly state that the run stopped short of the planned episodes nor explain the stopping reason relative to the preregistered stopping rule. This must be disclosed and linked to the missingness handling already described.

Sampling / sampling-semantics disclosure: model_configuration.json lists temperature=null. The manuscript must explicitly report sampling settings literally (null/unset is not evidence of temperature=0) and explain how the shared_initial_candidate semantics were implemented (how the same sampled initial candidate was reused across paired conditions, and how repair calls were applied) so readers can interpret within-pair vs between-condition variance.

Disclosure Statement presentation: the Disclosure Statement currently includes run-internal paths and many full hashes in ordinary manuscript prose. Per the track guidance, condense the Disclosure Statement in the paper (keep mandatory content) and point readers to the archived evidence bundle for low-level paths/hashes rather than embedding them inline.

Citation & preregistration fidelity: the manuscript must ensure every in-text claim is supported by the cited record and use standard IEEE numbered citation markers in main prose. The provided evidence-verification metadata looks good, but the manuscript should explicitly present numbered citations and confirm that each cited item supports the adjacent claim.
required_revisions: Clarify and correct the primary-estimand definition and all labels of the binary outcome: explicitly state whether 'success' = (unsafe configuration accepted) or 'success' = (valid/safe configuration accepted). Recompute or relabel the reported paired counts/contingency table and the inferential language so that the sign/direction of the paired difference and the conclusion about H1 consistently match the preregistered hypothesis. Use only archived analysis artifacts to support any corrected wording (no new model calls).

Explicitly disclose the status of all preregistered secondary/auxiliary analyses and controls (particularly the benign-control M=50 and the false-positive blocking-rate estimand). If those runs were not executed, state that they were not executed and mark them as unperformed preregistered items (Methods and Results). If results exist in the archived bundle, add the reported secondary results or link to their archived analysis files with hashes (do not add new experiments).

Add an explicit statement in Methods and Disclosure that planned_episode_count=300 but completed_episode_count=282, explain why the run stopped early (provider/API/infrastructure constraint per the preregistered stopping rule), and confirm that the preregistered missingness handling was applied (point to the missingness_summary artifact and show how exclusions were applied).

Report sampling semantics exactly as archived: state that temperature was null/unset in model_configuration.json, explain what that implies for hosted-model sampling in this execution, and document how the shared_initial_candidate policy was implemented in practice (cite provider_call_audit and shared_initial_candidate traces). If the shared initial candidate was used to produce paired baseline/guarded comparisons, state this clearly and explain how repair calls were allocated across conditions.

Condense the Disclosure Statement in the manuscript body: remove run-internal file paths and full hashes from ordinary prose, keep required items (models, framework, initial master prompt reference, autonomy boundary, preregistration SHA), and add a concise pointer to the archived evidence bundle where full manifests and hashes are available (preserve archival references but not detailed path lists in the main text).

Ensure in-text citations use IEEE numbered markers and that each referenced work actually supports the adjacent claims. Where a claim relies on a specific prior result, replace any generic URL/DOI insertions in prose with numbered references and, if necessary, a short parenthetical that identifies which part of the cited work supports the statement. (This is a presentation/formatting clarification resolvable from the archived bibliography.)
optional_revisions: Provide a short clarifying paragraph or table describing the six discordant pairs (n10=6) in anonymized form (referencing archived validator traces) to illustrate the mechanism by which the guarded pipeline changed outcomes (sanitizer vs repair vs gating). This is optional but would strengthen interpretability and failure-mode analysis.

Report the preregistered sensitivity analyses already present in the archive (failure-as-zero, bootstrap variants, and false-positive blocking on any available benign-control runs) as supplementary materials or appendix within the five-page limit if space permits.

Tighten the Discussion on practical significance: accompany the statistical result with an explicit statement about absolute effect size relevance in operational terms (e.g., expected deployments avoided per 1000 adversarial intents) and emphasize limitations for production deployment strategies.
